title: Vaporize inventory/status/warehouse must use DirectoryTools discovery
createdBy: codex loom harness per operator correction: vaporize-owned errors belong in vaporize

historicalContent.problem: Vaporize mode status/warehouse/inventory currently owns a private recursive JSON filesystem walk in Sources/vaporize-cli/VaporInventory.swift. This duplicates DirectoryTools traversal policy and risks inconsistent pruning, long scans, and future drift from shared discovery behavior.
observedEvidence: Sources/vaporize-cli/VaporInventory.swift uses FileManager.enumerator directly to scan every .json file.
directory-tools@swift-universal.cli already owns shared traversal services and documents the naive-walk anti-pattern.
A related vaporware local --all discovery attempt exposed the same class of bug: consumer tools should not invent filesystem walkers when shared DirectoryTools primitives exist.
requiredFix: Add directory-tools@swift-universal.cli as a Vaporize dependency where needed.
Replace VaporInventoryScanner's private recursive JSON enumeration with DirectoryTools DirectoryFileDiscoveryService or a successor shared API.
Preserve VaporInventoryScanner classification behavior and receipt shape.
Add/keep tests proving recursive JSON discovery, ignored/generated-directory pruning, missing-path errors, file-path errors, and receipt totals.
Do not change list-targets project-root behavior; list-targets remains Vaporize's app target truth once a project root is supplied.
acceptanceCriteria: Vaporize has no direct recursive FileManager.enumerator path for inventory/status/warehouse JSON discovery.
Vaporize CUJ-07 inventory tests pass against DirectoryTools-backed discovery.
The scanner still resolves relative paths to absolute standardized paths.
The warehouse receipt remains machine-readable and schema-compatible.
The bug cross-references the shared DirectoryTools consumer bead.
